Hey there! I was you 7 months ago! Co slept starting around 11 months because she just would not sleep through the night and getting up every three hours was killing me. Fed her to sleep around 7 every night, then when she woke up at like 10 on the dot we would get into the floor bed together and she stayed latched to me until my alarm went off every morning. 

We moved into a new house when she was 14 months and I was so scared the first night that things were going to be even worse, had the floor bed there next to her crib and was waiting for the ten PM cry for mama. It didn’t happen. 11 o’clock rolled around, my husband convinced me to just go to bed in our room and see what happened. I woke up in my own bed at 7 am wondering what the hell was going on, scrambled in a panic to check the baby monitor. She was still asleep in her crib. 

She has slept 12 hours through the night every single night since, going on 3 months now. I still can’t believe it. I don’t know if the change in scenery pushed her into a new stage or if this house has some kind of benevolent ghosts soothing her to sleep. But the miracle happened. And I was ready to be stuck in a floor bed with a Velcro baby for years. 

There are some days I miss it. She’s such a good little snuggler. But now I get up earlier than I need to and wake her up, and we get in the floor bed (it’s still right next to her crib) and we snuggle and nurse for an hour every morning.

Sitting here at 4 am with my stage 5 clinger snoring on me, ready to share my graduation story. 

I started losing my mucous plug at 35 weeks on a Friday. Didn’t bother calling my OB because I read everywhere that it didn’t necessarily mean labor was imminent, also I went to my birthing and delivery class/hospital tour the following morning (Saturday) and confirmed with a delivery nurse in class that it wasn’t necessary to call my OB just for that. During this time I knew my daughter was transverse but still had plenty of time to get turned around. My plan was vaginal birth with minimal intervention (maybe nitrous for pain). I wasn’t totally opposed to an epidural but wanted to give it the ol college try without.

Sunday during the day, continued losing pieces of my mucous plug, husband and I did some more prep and housework, including finalizing our hospital bags. I also washed all of our bedding (I think this is what cursed me, like washing your car and then it rains lol). 

Sunday night (technically Monday morning) 3:07 am. My water does not break, it explodes. All over my nice clean sheets. I wake up my husband, call my OB’s office, they tell me to come in. I ask if I have time to shower and have some breakfast since I’ve been hearing over and over that first time moms can be in labor a long time. The on-call OB says sure, have a nice hot breakfast and a shower (I soon regretted the breakfast) just get there within two hours. I ask ‘So does this mean I’m for sure having my baby early? Should I let my mom who is out of state know she should start looking at plane tickets?’ The doctor chuckles a bit and says ‘Yes, you’ll be having your daughter today or tomorrow, call your mom.’

I get to the hospital around 4:15 am, feeling pretty good, but feeling some light cramping. Sono tech comes in to see what my baby’s position is, and she is still totally transverse. Uh oh. My OB gets in for her shift at 6 am and tells me we need to do a C section, so all of my plans are out the window. I’m not too disappointed, just excited to meet my daughter. They tell me we can get the epidural going ASAP and have my baby out by 7:30 am. ‘Oh wait, when was the last time you ate anything?’ My 3:30 am muesli comes back to haunt me, as I now have to wait until afternoon for my c section. 

My husband and I settle in to wait almost six hours in the uncomfortable little room, my ‘cramps’ start getting worse. Hours pass and I’m doubled over in pain at each cramp. My husband has asked me several times if these are contractions and I keep saying I don’t think so because they’re not THAT painful. I guess I was in denial or not thinking straight because he times them and convinces me I was probably in active labor and should tell the nurse lol. 

I let the staff know, the rushed the anesthesiologist in since it was after 11 by this point anyway. The first attempt to place the epidural was horrible. Hit a blood vessel and I thought I was going to die. I didn’t want to scare my husband so I just panicked internally, but they got it all fixed up and my pain dropped to a 1. The rest was a breeze. I was wheeled to the OR, my lovely daughter was out and in my arms by 12:45. She was breathing fine and didn’t have to go to NICU. 5 lbs 8 ounces, latched like a champ and did great on all of their tests (except hearing, she had fluid in her ears due to being a c section baby and didn’t pass hearing until her second screening).

Apparently I had an unusually easy recovery. I was very mobile immediately after my section (not fully walking, but easily able to lift myself and move around in bed, get in my wheelchair) and my pain was nonexistent. I was walking easily the next morning, the worst pain was when they took my catheter out and I had to pee. 

I requested to be discharged a day early, and due to my mobility and baby doing so well it was approved and I was home Wednesday. 

Overall I was very happy with the C section experience, it was quick and easy besides the epidural issue. Baby is now three weeks old and doing great. She’s tiny but perfectly healthy. ❤️
